Haha yeah it's kinda funny. I had a bunch of local news coverage back in 2014 on my Elysium exoskeleton project, and since then I've done way cooler and more complicated stuff, but nothing really "news worthy". 

This media blitz was actually thanks to YouTube Canada PR reaching out to local news places to say, hey this guy does cool stuff, EndGame comes out this week, you should interview him! And so, I was on CP24 breakfast, Your Morning, and eTalk today as well! Feels good to get recognition, though cross platform, we won't really see any increase on YouTube -- BUT, it definitely helps put us on the map so to speak, with Canadians being like oh, he's from here!
Surprise!

When you get bigger on YouTube you do end up having a bit more protection from YouTube, and real people to talk to for help, but all those issues you listed do exist. We do try and keep a diverse income stream to minimize risk like that. Still waiting for a YouTube competitor to shake things up.

Just wondering, why do you think we don't? 

All of our employees, and co-ops are paid well. Highschool co-ops are not, as they only get a credit if it is unpaid.
That's a different short term role we're playing with. It has many benefits beyond pay. Launching your own YouTube channel, access to our resources for your own passion projects, etc :)

I was able to add more filters to my moderation queue, so, while I didn't solve it fully, I still likely saved hundreds to thousands of fans from getting spoiled while watching my video. So, I think that's a a win still.

It also enables someone to get experience when we can't actually as a business justify another hire in that specific role at the moment ;)  also the majority of our core team all started as volunteers, as that's how this business started :)
